## Statement and geometric setting

Cañete, Miranda Jr., and Vittone study the isoperimetric problem for the lower-semicontinuous planar strip density and identify a symmetric four-arc family among the possible candidates. Their Conjecture 3.12 predicts that type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) candidates are never minimizing; the relevant geometric classification and the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\)/type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) formulas occur in §3.2, especially Lemma 3.8 and equations (26)–(27) of the cited paper.

Fix \(\lambda>1\). On \(\mathbb R^2\), set

\[
f_\lambda(x,y)=
\begin{cases}
1,& |y|\leq 1,\\
\lambda,& |y|>1,
\end{cases}
\qquad
A_\lambda(E)=\int_E f_\lambda\,d\mathcal L^2,
\qquad
P_\lambda(E)=\int_{\partial E} f_\lambda\,d\mathcal H^1.
\]

Here the boundary is the complete topological frontier of the Euclidean realization of the coordinate carrier, not a freely chosen list of arcs. The formal modeled regions carry the integrability hypotheses needed for the area and frontier integrals, and the admissible competitor type compares the candidate with empty, general, four-arc, and replacement carriers. [@lean:StripDensity] [@lean:WeightedArea] [@lean:FrontierMeasure] [@lean:WeightedPerimeter] [@lean:FinitePerimeterRegion] [@lean:AdmissibleCompetitor] [@lean:AdmissibleCompetitor.weightedArea_eq_carrier] [@lean:AdmissibleCompetitor.WeightedPerimeter]

A modeled four-arc candidate has curvature and exterior half-angle satisfying

\[
0<h\leq1,
\qquad
0<\alpha<\frac{\pi}{2},
\qquad
\lambda\cos\alpha=h.
\]

Its common radius is \(R=1/h\); the upper and lower exterior caps have chord length \(2R\sin\alpha\) on the two density-one interfaces, and the strip core contributes two circular side arcs. The formal CMV predicate consists exactly of the density jump and Snell incidence. It does not assume an area formula, a competitor, or nonminimality. The incidence equation selects the principal inverse-cosine branch:

\[\alpha=\arccos(h/\lambda).\]

The analytic arguments use \(0<h<1\), while the candidate constructor retains the finite closure value \(h=1\). [@lean:FourArcCandidate] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.capChord] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.stripCore] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.assembly] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.SatisfiesCMVTypeIVHypotheses] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.alpha_eq_arccos]

**Theorem.** For every \(\lambda>1\), every modeled regular type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) four-arc candidate satisfying the formal CMV type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) hypotheses fails to minimize weighted perimeter. Explicitly, the assertion

\[
\forall F\text{ admissible},\quad
A_\lambda(F)=A_\lambda(E)\Longrightarrow P_\lambda(E)\leq P_\lambda(F)
\]

is false for the modeled candidate \(E\). The formal root has precisely this all-density modeled scope and includes the constructor's closure endpoint through the proved formula identities; it does not introduce a source-level normalization theorem. [@lean:FourArcCandidate.IsWeightedPerimeterMinimizer] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_density_gt_one]

## Scalar formulas and geometric realization

For the analytic comparison, write

\[
B(x)=\lambda\arccos(x/\lambda)+\arcsin x,
\qquad
D(x)=\frac{\sqrt{\lambda^2-x^2}}{\lambda}-\sqrt{1-x^2},
\qquad
q(h)=2h-1.
\]

The scalar areas and perimeters are

\[
\begin{aligned}
A_4(h)&=\frac{2\bigl(B(h)+hD(h)\bigr)}{h^2},
&P_4(h)&=\frac{4B(h)}{h},\\
A_3(h)&=\frac{B(q(h))+\pi/2+(q(h)+2)D(q(h))}{h^2},
&P_3(h)&=\frac{2\bigl(B(q(h))+\pi/2+D(q(h))\bigr)}{h}.
\end{aligned}
\]

The geometric type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier uses \(0<h<1\); the type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) candidate uses \(0<h\leq1\). Formula values at a closure point are not silently treated as a regular carrier. [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeShape] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeAngle] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeDelta] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreePerimeter] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourAngle] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourDelta] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourArea] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourPerimeter]

For a regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) competitor at curvature \(h\), put

\[
R=\frac1h,
\qquad \beta=\arccos q(h),
\qquad \alpha=\arccos\!\bigl(q(h)/\lambda\bigr),
\qquad w=R\bigl(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta\bigr).
\]

The carrier is the union of a rectangle \([-w,w]\times[-1,1]\), two strip-side circular segments, and an upper circular cap. Its complete frontier is the two strip-side arcs, the upper cap arc, and the bottom horizontal segment. The bottom segment is allowed to degenerate at \(h=1/2\); the upper cap is branch-complete, so major, semicircular, and minor cases are all represented. [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.coreCarrier] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.outerCap] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.carrier] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.bottomSegmentCarrier] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.bottomChord]

A circular cap of radius \(R\) and half-central angle \(\theta\in(0,\pi)\) has Euclidean area and arc length

\[
R^2\bigl(\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta\bigr)
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
2R\theta,
\]

respectively. The formal Hausdorff-measure identities identify these lengths with the Euclidean \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure of the actual arc traces. Finite junction sets have zero one-dimensional measure, so the complete-frontier integrals are exactly the sums of the displayed component contributions. [@lean:OneSidedCircularCap.volume_carrier] [@lean:cap_arcLength_eq_two_radius_theta] [@lean:exact_euclidean_capTrace_hausdorffMeasure] [@lean:exact_euclidean_leftArcTrace_hausdorffMeasure] [@lean:exact_euclidean_rightArcTrace_hausdorffMeasure] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.exact_euclidean_bottomSegmentCarrier_hausdorffMeasure] [@lean:fourArc_euclidean_frontier] [@lean:fourArc_frontier_weightedPerimeter_eq] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.euclidean_frontier] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.weightedPerimeter_eq_modeledWeightedPerimeter]

The type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier is therefore a genuine measurable, integrable admissible competitor. Its geometric area and perimeter reduce to \(A_3(h)\) and \(P_3(h)\), while the candidate's complete-frontier area and perimeter reduce to \(A_4(h)\) and \(P_4(h)\). [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.TypeThreeAssembly.scalarWeightedArea_eq_typeThreeArea] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.TypeThreeAssembly.scalarWeightedPerimeter_eq_typeThreePerimeter] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.weightedArea_eq_typeFourArea] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.weightedPerimeter_eq_typeFourPerimeter] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.weightedArea_formula] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.weightedPerimeter_formula] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.integrableOn_carrier] [@lean:TypeThreeAssembly.integrable_frontierMeasure]

## Fold monotonicity and the stationary pair

On \(0<h<1\), define

\[
\begin{aligned}
F_4(h)&=4\left[h\left(\frac1{\sqrt{1-h^2}}-\frac\lambda{\sqrt{\lambda^2-h^2}}\right)-B(h)\right],\\
F_3(h)&=4h\left[\frac{1+q(h)}{\sqrt{1-q(h)^2}}-\frac{\lambda^2+q(h)}{\lambda\sqrt{\lambda^2-q(h)^2}}\right]\\
&\qquad-2\left[B(q(h))+\frac\pi2+D(q(h))\right].
\end{aligned}
\]

Differentiation gives

\[
A_i'(h)=\frac{F_i(h)}{h^3},
\qquad
P_i'(h)=hA_i'(h),
\qquad i\in\{3,4\}.
\]

Thus the fold zeros are stationary points of the area profiles; stationarity is used to choose a comparison pair, not assumed of the candidate being excluded. [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeFold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourFold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.hasDerivAt_typeThreeArea] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.hasDerivAt_typeFourArea] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThree_variational_hasDerivAt] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFour_variational_hasDerivAt]

For \(-1<x<1\), the radical-cube gap

\[
K(x)=\frac1{(1-x^2)^{3/2}}-\frac\lambda{(\lambda^2-x^2)^{3/2}}
\]

is positive whenever \(\lambda>1\). Consequently \(F_3\) and \(F_4\) are strictly increasing on their regular domains. In particular, \(A_3\) has at most one fold transition, so its value on a compact interval is bounded by the larger endpoint value. [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.radicalCubeGap_pos] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.hasDerivAt_typeThreeFold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.hasDerivAt_typeFourFold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeFold_strictMonoOn] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourFold_strictMonoOn] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_le_max_endpoints]

To avoid evaluating the singular expression \(F_4(1)\), clear its positive radical denominators with

\[
C(h)=h\bigl(\sqrt{\lambda^2-h^2}-\lambda\sqrt{1-h^2}\bigr)-B(h)\sqrt{1-h^2}\sqrt{\lambda^2-h^2}.
\]

This function is continuous through \(h=1\), agrees with a positive multiple of \(F_4\) on \(0<h<1\), is negative at \(h=9/10\), and is positive at \(h=1\). Hence some \(s\in(9/10,1)\) satisfies \(F_4(s)=0\). Strict fold monotonicity then gives

\[
A_4(s)\leq A_4(h)
\qquad(0<h\leq1).
\]

At the closure endpoint, the argument uses continuity of the finite area formula; it does not use an endpoint derivative of the singular raw fold. [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourClearedFold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourClearedFold_continuous] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourClearedFold_eq_fold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourClearedFold_multiplier_pos] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourClearedFold_nine_tenths_neg] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourClearedFold_one_pos] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourFold_zero_exists] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourArea_fold_le]

## Equal-area comparison and the envelope

The same-curvature comparison is strict:

\[
A_3(h)<A_4(h)
\qquad(\lambda>1,\quad 0<h\leq1).
\]

A support-function argument also gives, for \(1/2<h<1\),

\[
P_3(h)-hA_3(h)<P_4(h)-hA_4(h).
\]

If \(1/2<r<h<1\) and \(A_3(r)=A_4(h)=V\), introduce the support-transfer function

\[H_V(x)=P_3(x)+x\bigl(V-A_3(x)\bigr).\]

The function \(H_V\) is nondecreasing from \(r\) to \(h\). Combining this with the support inequality yields

\[
P_3(r)<P_4(h),
\]

and the increasing-fold argument yields \(F_3(r)<0\). [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_lt_typeFourArea] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourSupport] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourSupport_hasDerivAt] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourSupport_concaveOn] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourSupport_one_gt_halfPi] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourSupport_midpoint] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.sameHeight_support_identity] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThree_support_lt_typeFour_support] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeAreaSupport] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeAreaSupport_hasDerivAt] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreePerimeter_lt_typeFourPerimeter_of_equalArea] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeFold_neg_of_equalArea_of_lt]

The endpoint values

\[
A_3(1/2)=2\pi(\lambda+1),
\qquad
A_4(1)<A_3(1/2)
\]

bracket the stationary target \(A_4(s)\). Continuity therefore produces \(r\in(1/2,s)\) with

\[
A_3(r)=A_4(s),
\qquad F_3(r)<0,
\qquad P_3(r)<P_4(s).
\]

Equivalently, there is a stationary equal-area pair with a strictly better type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) member for every \(\lambda>1\). [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_half] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeFourArea_one_lt_typeThreeArea_half] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.stationaryEqualAreaPair_of_typeFourFold_zero] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.stationaryEqualAreaPair_exists] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.stationaryEqualAreaPair_strictImprovement_exists]

Fix such a pair \((r,s)\). Since \(A_3(h)\to+\infty\) as \(h\downarrow0\), strict decrease on the negative-fold branch supplies, for every \(h\in(0,1]\), a unique descending root \(\rho(h)\) satisfying

\[
A_3(\rho(h))=A_4(h),
\qquad F_3(\rho(h))<0.
\]

The root obeys \(\rho(h)<h\), is continuous on \((0,1]\), and is differentiable in the interior with

\[
\rho'(h)=\frac{A_4'(h)}{A_3'(\rho(h))}.
\]

[@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_tendsto_atRight_zero] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_strictAntiOn_Icc_of_fold_neg_right] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_descending_root_existsUnique] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_descending_root_existsUnique_of_stationary_pair] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.typeThreeArea_descending_root_lt] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.equalAreaRoot_continuousOn_of_compact_unique] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.equalAreaRoot_hasDerivAt]

Define the equal-area perimeter gap

\[
\Delta(h)=P_3(\rho(h))-P_4(h).
\]

The variational identities give

\[
\Delta'(h)=(\rho(h)-h)A_4'(h).
\]

The first factor is negative, while \(A_4'\) changes sign only at \(s\). Thus \(\Delta\) reaches its maximum at \(s\), and

\[
\Delta(h)\leq\Delta(s)=P_3(r)-P_4(s)<0
\qquad(0<h\leq1).
\]

This is the all-curvature step: the stationary pair controls the envelope, but the excluded candidate may have any modeled curvature in its formal range. [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.equalAreaPerimeterGap] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.equalAreaPerimeterGap_hasDerivAt] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.equalAreaPerimeterGap_lt_fold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.equalAreaPerimeterGap_le_fold] [@lean:LeanSuffixAnalytic.allCurvature_typeThreeImprovement_of_envelope]

For the candidate at curvature \(h\), use the regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly at \(\rho(h)\). The carrier realization gives exactly equal weighted area and strictly smaller complete-frontier weighted perimeter, so substituting it into the definition of modeled minimality is contradictory. [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_analytic_typeThree] [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_stationaryEqualAreaPair] [@lean:FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_typeThree]

## Closing scope

This all-density theorem subsumes the earlier modeled cutoff \(\lambda\geq51/50\) and closes the entire modeled interval \(1<\lambda<51/50\). The root concerns precisely modeled regular type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) four-arc candidates satisfying the formal hypotheses, with the formal constructor's closure endpoint handled by the proved branch-complete identities. It does not claim the unqualified source-level CMV Conjecture 3.12.

Two separate bridges remain outside this root: normalization of every source-defined type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) region into the formal candidate, and compatibility between CMV's reduced-boundary perimeter and the model's complete-frontier perimeter for the candidate and the constructed competitor. A universal classification of every arbitrary minimizer is stronger than the bridge needed for this modeled theorem; the present result needs only the identified modeled candidate and one validated equal-area, lower-perimeter competitor. [@lean:CMVSuffixModel.FourArcCandidate.not_isWeightedPerimeterMinimizer_of_density_gt_one]

The supplement records the mathematical meanings of every declaration in the frozen publication closure. The assembled ledger is ordered alphabetically by declaration name within two classification blocks: the first contains the \(192\) declarations classified as main, and the second contains the \(272\) declarations classified as supplement. Each entry separates its mathematical statement and explanation from the declaration name, source location, and Lean code supplied as metadata by the renderer.

The notation is as follows. The density is \(f_\lambda\), weighted area and complete-frontier weighted perimeter are \(A_\lambda\) and \(P_\lambda\), and \(B,D,q,A_3,P_3,A_4,P_4,F_3,F_4\) have the meanings stated in the main proof. Unless an entry states a larger domain, analytic comparisons use \(\lambda>1\) and regular curvatures in \((0,1)\); endpoint identities are stated separately when they are valid. A cap has chord \(L>0\), half-central angle \(0<\theta<\pi\), midpoint \((m,b)\), and radius \(R=L/(2\sin\theta)\). Write \(a(\theta)=(\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta)/(4\sin^2\theta)\) and \(\ell(\theta)=\theta/\sin\theta\). A regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly uses \(R=1/h\), \(q=2h-1\), \(\beta=\arccos q\), \(\alpha=\arccos(q/\lambda)\), \(\gamma=\pi-\beta\), and \(w=R(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta)\). All Hausdorff measures in the ledger are Euclidean; coordinate carriers and their Euclidean images are distinguished explicitly.

No generated declaration families are configured in this frozen package, and no inventoried declaration is marked generated. Accordingly the generated-family list is empty. Repetitive algebra, endpoint arithmetic, parametrization plumbing, and integrability transport remain in the declaration-level ledger; the main proof retains the conceptual geometric and analytic argument. classifications.informal_statement: The coordinate point space is \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This abbreviation supplies ordered real coordinates; it does not itself select the Euclidean norm used for perimeter.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean realization of the coordinate plane has the norm \(\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The underlying pairs are unchanged, but the metric for Hausdorff measure is the Euclidean product norm.

classifications.informal_statement: The map \(J\) identifies the coordinate plane homeomorphically with its Euclidean realization.
classifications.latex_explanation: It sends each coordinate pair to the identical pair with the Euclidean norm; it is a homeomorphism, not a claim that every product metric agrees with that norm.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip density is \(f_\lambda(x,y)=1\) for \(\lvert y\rvert\leq1\), and \(f_\lambda(x,y)=\lambda\) otherwise.
classifications.latex_explanation: Both interfaces have density one. The definition permits any real density parameter; the main theorem requires \(\lambda>1\).

classifications.informal_statement: The weighted area of a carrier \(E\) is \(A_\lambda(E)=\int_E f_\lambda\,d\mathcal L^2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is a real integral over the coordinate carrier; the geometric realization proves integrability rather than assuming a scalar area.

classifications.informal_statement: The frontier measure of \(E\) is the pullback under \(J\) of \(\mathcal H^1\) restricted to \(\partial J(E)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Explicitly, the measure is \((J^{-1})_*(\mathcal H^1\big|_{\partial J(E)})\). The complete Euclidean frontier, not the reduced boundary, is used.

classifications.informal_statement: For a boundary measure \(\mu\), weighted perimeter is \(\int f_\lambda\,d\mu\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The definition accepts an arbitrary measure; canonical carrier perimeter is obtained by using the frontier measure.

classifications.informal_statement: A general modeled region consists of a measurable carrier with integrable density over its area and against its frontier measure.
classifications.latex_explanation: These are precisely the two finiteness obligations stored with the carrier. The name does not assert a separate bounded-variation or reduced-boundary definition.

classifications.informal_statement: The weighted area of a general modeled region is the weighted integral over its stored carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: No independent area value is stored: this operation applies \(A_\lambda\) to the carrier.

classifications.informal_statement: A cap side is either upper or lower.
classifications.latex_explanation: This two-element choice determines which closed half-plane is intersected with the cap's disk.

classifications.informal_statement: A one-sided circular cap is specified by \(L>0\), \(0<\theta<\pi\), a chord midpoint \((m,b)\), and a choice of side.
classifications.latex_explanation: The radius, center, carrier, and boundary arc are derived. The interval includes minor, semicircular, and major caps.

classifications.informal_statement: A cap with chord \(L\) and half-central angle \(\theta\) has radius \(R=L/(2\sin\theta)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The angular bounds make the denominator strictly positive and give the usual chord relation.

classifications.informal_statement: The upper cap center is \((m,b-R\cos\theta)\), and the lower cap center is \((m,b+R\cos\theta)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The vertical sign selects which side of the chord contains the cap, including the major-cap case.

classifications.informal_statement: The cap arc is parameterized by \((m+R\sin t,b\pm R(\cos t-\cos\theta))\), with the plus sign for the upper side.
classifications.latex_explanation: The intended angular interval is \([-\theta,\theta]\); the formula itself is defined for every real \(t\).

classifications.informal_statement: The left endpoint of a cap is \((m-L/2,b)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the left end of the horizontal chord, independently of the cap side.

classifications.informal_statement: The right endpoint of a cap is \((m+L/2,b)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the right end of the horizontal chord, independently of the cap side.

classifications.informal_statement: The squared distance of \(p\) from the cap center \(c\) is \((p_1-c_1)^2+(p_2-c_2)^2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This coordinate polynomial defines the disk inequality without invoking the product-space metric.

classifications.informal_statement: The cap carrier is its closed disk intersected with \(y\geq b\) for an upper cap or \(y\leq b\) for a lower cap.
classifications.latex_explanation: The disk is centered as specified above and has radius \(R\). This is the actual planar set whose area and arc trace are computed.

classifications.informal_statement: The interior cap carrier uses strict disk and strict side inequalities.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the intersection of the open disk with the chosen open half-plane; its inclusion in the carrier interior is proved separately.

classifications.informal_statement: The chord carrier is \(\{(x,b):\lvert x-m\rvert\leq L/2\}\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It includes both endpoints and is shared by the upper and lower cap descriptions.

classifications.informal_statement: The cap's scalar Euclidean area is \(L^2a(\theta)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Since \(L=2R\sin\theta\), this equals \(R^2(\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta)\); equality with carrier volume is a theorem.

classifications.informal_statement: The cap's scalar arc length is \(L\ell(\theta)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The chord-radius relation turns this into \(2R\theta\); later results identify it with Euclidean Hausdorff length.

classifications.informal_statement: For every cap, \(\sin\theta>0\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This follows from \(0<\theta<\pi\) and justifies division by the sine.

classifications.informal_statement: Every cap radius is strictly positive.
classifications.latex_explanation: Both the chord and the denominator \(2\sin\theta\) are positive.

classifications.informal_statement: Every cap's scalar Euclidean area is strictly positive.
classifications.latex_explanation: The factor \(L^2\) is positive and \(a(\theta)>0\) throughout the cap-angle domain.

classifications.informal_statement: For every cap, \(\ell(\theta)>0\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The quotient \(\theta/\sin\theta\) has positive numerator and denominator.

classifications.informal_statement: Every cap's scalar arc length is strictly positive.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the product of the positive chord length and positive normalized arc length.

classifications.informal_statement: The cap radius satisfies \(R\sin\theta=L/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This identity relates the trigonometric parameterization to the geometric chord endpoints.

classifications.informal_statement: At \(t=-\theta\), the cap arc reaches the left endpoint.
classifications.latex_explanation: Oddness of sine and the chord-radius identity give horizontal coordinate \(m-L/2\); the vertical displacement vanishes.

classifications.informal_statement: At \(t=\theta\), the cap arc reaches the right endpoint.
classifications.latex_explanation: The chord-radius identity gives horizontal coordinate \(m+L/2\), and the point lies on the base line.

classifications.informal_statement: For \(\lvert t\rvert\leq\theta\), the cap arc lies in its chosen closed half-plane.
classifications.latex_explanation: On this angular interval, \(\cos t\geq\cos\theta\); the vertical sign distinguishes the upper and lower statements.

classifications.informal_statement: For \(\lvert t\rvert<\theta\), the cap arc lies in its chosen open half-plane.
classifications.latex_explanation: The strict cosine inequality separates all interior arc points from the chord line.

classifications.informal_statement: A cap-carrier point on the base line belongs to the chord carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: Substituting \(y=b\) into the disk inequality bounds the horizontal displacement by \(L/2\).

classifications.informal_statement: The chord carrier is contained in the cap carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: The chord inequality implies the disk inequality, and the base line satisfies either closed side condition.

classifications.informal_statement: Every cap carrier is measurable.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is described by continuous polynomial inequalities and a closed half-plane condition.

classifications.informal_statement: Every cap carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: The disk and the chosen half-plane are closed, so their intersection is closed.

classifications.latex_explanation: The point is obtained by translating the midpoint right by half the chord length.

classifications.informal_statement: The scalar Euclidean length of the horizontal segment is \(L\).

classifications.informal_statement: A strip core is specified by \(L>0\) and \(0<\kappa\leq1\).

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core radius is \(R=1/\kappa\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The curvature bound implies \(R\geq1\), so the circle can span the strip height.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core side angle is \(\phi=\arcsin\kappa\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The principal arcsine gives \(0<\phi\leq\pi/2\).

classifications.informal_statement: The left side-circle center has horizontal coordinate \(c_{\mathrm L}=-L/2+R\cos\phi\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Its vertical coordinate is zero; the circle meets the left chord endpoints at heights \(\pm1\).

classifications.informal_statement: The right side-circle center has horizontal coordinate \(c_{\mathrm R}=L/2-R\cos\phi\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the reflection of the left center across the vertical axis.

classifications.informal_statement: The core rectangle is \([-L/2,L/2]\times[-1,1]\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This central rectangle joins the two circular side pieces and has area \(2L\).

classifications.informal_statement: The left core piece is the disk \((x-c_{\mathrm L})^2+y^2\leq R^2\) restricted to \(x\leq-L/2\) and \(\lvert y\rvert\leq1\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Only the outer left circular segment is retained; the rectangle occupies the remaining central portion.

classifications.informal_statement: The right core piece is the disk \((x-c_{\mathrm R})^2+y^2\leq R^2\) restricted to \(x\geq L/2\) and \(\lvert y\rvert\leq1\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the reflected right circular segment adjoining the rectangle.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core carrier is the union of its rectangle and its two side pieces.
classifications.latex_explanation: The construction defines an actual closed coordinate set within the strip rather than an assigned area-perimeter pair.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip core's scalar area is \(2L+8a(\phi)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Each side segment has chord length two and hence area \(4a(\phi)\); the rectangle contributes \(2L\).

classifications.informal_statement: The total length of the core's two curved sides is \(4\ell(\phi)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Each side arc has chord two and length \(2\ell(\phi)=2R\phi\); the interface chords are not counted here.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core radius is positive.
classifications.latex_explanation: This follows from the strictly positive curvature in the constructor.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core side angle is positive.
classifications.latex_explanation: The principal arcsine is positive at a positive curvature.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core side angle satisfies \(\phi\leq\pi/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The upper curvature bound includes equality, so this assertion is deliberately non-strict.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core side angle satisfies \(\phi<\pi\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The sharper bound \(\phi\leq\pi/2\) places the side segment in the cap-angle domain.

classifications.informal_statement: The identity \(\sin\phi=\kappa\) holds for every strip core.
classifications.latex_explanation: The curvature lies in the principal inverse-sine domain.

classifications.informal_statement: The identity \(\cos\phi=\sqrt{1-\kappa^2}\) holds for every strip core.
classifications.latex_explanation: The cosine is nonnegative on the selected principal branch, including the zero endpoint cosine.

classifications.informal_statement: Every point of the strip-core carrier satisfies \(\lvert y\rvert\leq1\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Each constituent set includes the same vertical strip restriction.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core carrier is measurable.
classifications.latex_explanation: Measurability follows from the coordinate inequalities and closure under finite unions.

classifications.informal_statement: The cap arc trace is the circle \(\lVert p-c\rVert_2^2=R^2\) restricted to the chosen closed side of the base line.

classifications.informal_statement: The strict interior cap carrier is open.

classifications.informal_statement: The strict interior cap carrier lies in the topological interior of the closed cap carrier.

classifications.informal_statement: The complete cap frontier is the union of its arc trace and chord carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: No other boundary components occur; the endpoints may belong to both pieces.

classifications.informal_statement: The left core arc trace is \((x-c_{\mathrm L})^2+y^2=R^2\), with \(x\leq-L/2\) and \(\lvert y\rvert\leq1\).

classifications.informal_statement: The upper chord trace is \(\{(x,1):\lvert x\rvert\leq L/2\}\).

classifications.informal_statement: The lower chord trace is \(\{(x,-1):\lvert x\rvert\leq L/2\}\).

classifications.informal_statement: Every strip-core carrier is closed.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip-core frontier is the union of the two side arc traces and the upper and lower chord traces.

classifications.informal_statement: For a curve \(c\) and real endpoints \(a,b\), the interval pushforward is \(c_*(\mathcal L^1\text{ restricted to }[a,b])\).

classifications.informal_statement: A horizontal segment has arclength map \(s\mapsto(m+s,b)\).

classifications.informal_statement: The segment's ending parameter is \(L/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The parameter interval therefore has length equal to the chord.

classifications.informal_statement: A core side arc starts at parameter \(-R\phi\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The corresponding circular angle is \(-\phi\), with vertical coordinate \(-1\).

classifications.informal_statement: A core side arc ends at parameter \(R\phi\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The parameter span is \(2R\phi\) and the final vertical coordinate is one.

classifications.informal_statement: The left core arclength map is \((c_{\mathrm L}-R\cos(s/R),R\sin(s/R))\).

classifications.informal_statement: The right core arclength map is \((c_{\mathrm R}+R\cos(s/R),R\sin(s/R))\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It traces the reflected right outer side over the same parameter interval.

classifications.informal_statement: The left core boundary measure pushes interval length along the left core arclength map.
classifications.latex_explanation: The interval is \([-R\phi,R\phi]\); this measure counts only the left curved side.

classifications.informal_statement: The right core boundary measure pushes interval length along the right core arclength map.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the analogous measure on the right curved side, not on either chord.

classifications.informal_statement: Every point on the closed parameter interval of the left core arc has density one.
classifications.latex_explanation: Its vertical coordinate stays within the closed strip, including both interfaces.

classifications.informal_statement: Every point on the closed parameter interval of the right core arc has density one.
classifications.latex_explanation: The statement uses the same strip bound for the reflected arc.

classifications.informal_statement: The weighted integral along the left core boundary measure is \(2\ell(\phi)\), for every real \(\lambda\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The density is constantly one and the parameter interval has length \(2R\phi=2\ell(\phi)\).

classifications.informal_statement: The weighted integral along the right core boundary measure is \(2\ell(\phi)\), for every real \(\lambda\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the equal contribution of the reflected right curved side.

classifications.informal_statement: For \(0\leq\theta\leq\pi\), \(\int_{\cos\theta}^{1}\sqrt{1-x^2}\,dx=(\theta-\sin\theta\cos\theta)/2\).

classifications.informal_statement: Every horizontal line has zero planar Lebesgue measure.

classifications.informal_statement: Every vertical line has zero planar Lebesgue measure.

classifications.informal_statement: The rectangle in a strip core has planar volume \(2L\).

classifications.informal_statement: The right core circular piece has volume \(4a(\phi)\).

classifications.latex_explanation: The pieces overlap only on planar-null line segments, so their volumes add to the stored scalar area.

classifications.informal_statement: For every measurable curve and every real \(\lambda,a,b\), the strip density is integrable against the interval pushforward on \([a,b]\).

classifications.informal_statement: For every core and real \(\lambda\), the strip density is integrable against the left core boundary measure.

classifications.informal_statement: For every core and real \(\lambda\), the strip density is integrable against the right core boundary measure.

classifications.informal_statement: On any coordinate set of finite planar measure, the strip density is integrable for every real \(\lambda\).

classifications.informal_statement: The strip density is integrable over every cap carrier, for every real \(\lambda\).

classifications.informal_statement: The strip density is integrable over every strip-core carrier, for every real \(\lambda\).

classifications.informal_statement: For an upper cap based on \(y=1\), the weighted area is \(\lambda\) times its Euclidean area, for every real \(\lambda\).

classifications.informal_statement: For a lower cap based on \(y=-1\), the weighted area is \(\lambda\) times its Euclidean area, for every real \(\lambda\).

classifications.informal_statement: \(\sin\gamma=\sin\beta\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the sine complementary-angle identity for \(\gamma=\pi-\beta\).

classifications.informal_statement: \(\cos\gamma=-q\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the cosine identity for \(\gamma=\pi-\beta\), using \(\cos\beta=q\).

classifications.informal_statement: The auxiliary side cap is the lower one-sided cap with chord \(2R\sin\beta\), half-central angle \(\gamma\), midpoint \((0,1)\), and lower side.
classifications.latex_explanation: Its major-cap allowance packages the two congruent translated strip-side arcs into one cap whose area and arc length equal their sums.

classifications.informal_statement: The exterior cap is the upper one-sided cap with chord \(2R\sin\alpha\), half-central angle \(\alpha\), midpoint \((0,1)\), and upper side.
classifications.latex_explanation: The open angle range \(0<\alpha<\pi\) permits minor, semicircular, and major branches of the upper cap.

classifications.informal_statement: The complete type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier is the union of its core carrier and its upper exterior cap carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the actual coordinate set whose area and complete frontier are used in the admissible competitor.

classifications.informal_statement:
For a regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly with density \(\lambda>1\), curvature \(0<h<1\), and coordinate carrier \(E_3\), the weighted area is the ambient Lebesgue integral

\[
A_\lambda(E_3)=\int_{E_3} f_\lambda\,d\mathcal L^2.
\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The integration domain is the carrier \(E_3\), and the measure is two-dimensional Lebesgue measure restricted to that carrier. No frontier measure enters this definition. No scalar value is chosen independently of the carrier; the later area formula identifies this canonical quantity with \(A_3(h)\).

classifications.informal_statement:
For a regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly with density \(\lambda>1\), curvature \(0<h<1\), and coordinate carrier \(E_3\), let \(J\) be the coordinate-preserving homeomorphism to the Euclidean realization. The weighted perimeter is the complete-frontier integral

\[
P_\lambda(E_3)=\int_{\partial J(E_3)}(f_\lambda\circ J^{-1})\,d\mathcal H^1.
\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The boundary measure is Euclidean one-dimensional Hausdorff measure restricted to the complete topological frontier of \(J(E_3)\), transported back to the coordinate plane. No scalar value is chosen independently of the carrier; the later perimeter formula identifies this canonical quantity with \(P_3(h)\).

classifications.informal_statement: The rectangle contribution is \(4w\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The rectangle has width \(2w\) and height \(2\).

classifications.informal_statement: The modeled type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) weighted area is the rectangle area plus the lower-side cap area plus \(\lambda\) times the upper exterior-cap area.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is an explicit scalar expression derived from the actual carrier components; the formula theorem later identifies it with the canonical integral.

classifications.informal_statement: The modeled type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) perimeter is the lower side-cap arc length, \(\lambda\) times the upper cap arc length, and the bottom chord length.
classifications.latex_explanation: The bottom chord has density one and the exterior cap arc has density \(\lambda\); the two strip-side arcs are represented by the side-cap contribution.

classifications.informal_statement: The declaration defines the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) angle contribution \(\lambda\alpha+\pi-\beta\) or sine displacement \(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta\).
classifications.latex_explanation: These are the two geometric combinations that enter the area and perimeter formulas.

classifications.informal_statement: The declaration defines the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) angle contribution \(\lambda\alpha+\pi-\beta\) or sine displacement \(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta\).
classifications.latex_explanation: These are the two geometric combinations that enter the area and perimeter formulas.

classifications.informal_statement: The scalar type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) weighted-area formula is \[\frac{\lambda\alpha+\pi-\beta+(q+2)(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta)}{h^2}.\]
classifications.latex_explanation: This definition is the geometric angle-and-displacement expression after substituting the assembly parameters.

classifications.informal_statement: The scalar type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) weighted-perimeter formula is \[\frac{2\bigl(\lambda\alpha+\pi-\beta+\sin\alpha-\sin\beta\bigr)}{h}.\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The formula sums the two side traces, the density-weighted upper cap, and the bottom segment in the modeled normalization.

classifications.informal_statement: For every regular assembly, \(\sin\beta\leq\sin\alpha\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The density factor \(\lambda>1\) contracts the arccosine argument in absolute value, and the principal sine formula gives the non-strict comparison.

classifications.informal_statement: If \(h\ne1/2\), then \(\sin\beta<\sin\alpha\).
classifications.latex_explanation: At the only equality case the shape parameter is zero; excluding \(h=1/2\) makes the squared argument comparison strict.

classifications.informal_statement: The side half-width satisfies \(w\geq0\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the positive radius multiplied by \(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta\geq0\).
The strict sine comparison and positive radius give a nondegenerate horizontal expansion away from the semicircular transition.

classifications.informal_statement: \(w=0\) if and only if \(h=1/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The positive radius reduces vanishing of the half-width to equality of the two principal sines, which occurs exactly at zero shape.

classifications.informal_statement: The bottom chord parameter satisfies \(2w\geq0\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This follows from nonnegativity of the side half-width.

classifications.informal_statement: \(2w=0\) if and only if \(h=1/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The positive factor two preserves the exact vanishing condition for \(w\).
The bottom segment is nondegenerate on both open branches.

classifications.informal_statement: If \(h=1/2\), then \(\beta=\pi/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: At the transition the shape parameter is zero.

classifications.informal_statement: If \(h=1/2\), then \(\alpha=\pi/2\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The exterior argument is also zero at the same transition.

classifications.informal_statement: The outer cap has radius \(R\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Its chord is \(2R\sin\alpha\), so the cap radius formula cancels the positive sine factor.

classifications.informal_statement: The side cap has radius \(R\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Its chord is \(2R\sin\beta\), and \(\sin\gamma=\sin\beta\) makes the cap radius equal to the assembly radius.

classifications.informal_statement: The side cap center is \((0,R-1)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The lower-cap center formula with base line \(y=1\), angle \(\gamma\), and radius \(R\) gives this coordinate.

classifications.informal_statement: The left arc parametrization maps \([{-R\gamma},0]\) exactly onto the left arc trace.
classifications.latex_explanation: The interval covers the upper junction through the bottom point on every branch, including the semicircular transition.

classifications.informal_statement: The right arc parametrization maps \([0,R\gamma]\) exactly onto the right arc trace.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the reflected branch-complete parametrization from the bottom point to the upper junction.

classifications.informal_statement: For a center \(c\), the side-arc complex map is \(z\mapsto(c_x+\operatorname{Im}z,c_y-\operatorname{Re}z)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The map translates and rotates the standard complex circle into either side trace.

classifications.informal_statement: For every center \(c\), the side-arc complex map is an isometry from \(\mathbb C\) to the Euclidean plane.
classifications.latex_explanation: The coordinate expression preserves Euclidean distance.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized left arc parametrization is \(J(\operatorname{leftArcParam}(s))\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This transports the coordinate side trace to the Euclidean metric space.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized right arc parametrization is \(J(\operatorname{rightArcParam}(s))\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the corresponding definition for the right trace.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized left parametrization equals the side-arc complex isometry at the left center applied to \(\gamma_R(s)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The identity follows from the real and imaginary coordinates of the standard circle.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized right parametrization equals the side-arc complex isometry at the right center applied to \(\gamma_R(s)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the reflected pointwise realization identity.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized left arc parametrization is continuous on \(\mathbb R\).
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the composition of a continuous standard circle map with an isometry.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized right arc parametrization is continuous on \(\mathbb R\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The same composition argument applies to the right side.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized left arc image on \([{-R\gamma},0]\) equals the Euclidean image of the left arc trace.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the homeomorphic transport of the coordinate image theorem.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized right arc image on \([0,R\gamma]\) equals the Euclidean image of the right arc trace.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the corresponding transported right-trace equality.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean image of the left arc trace is measurable.
classifications.latex_explanation: The exact image is the compact continuous image of a closed bounded parameter interval, hence Borel measurable.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean image of the right arc trace is measurable.
classifications.latex_explanation: The same compact-parametrization argument applies to the right trace.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean left arc image has \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure \(\operatorname{ofReal}(R\gamma)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The parametrization interval has length \(R\gamma\), and the side-arc isometry preserves the exact Hausdorff mass.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean right arc image has \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure \(\operatorname{ofReal}(R\gamma)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The right trace has the same radius and angular span as the left trace.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean image of the left arc trace has \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure \(\operatorname{ofReal}(R\gamma)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The image equality transfers the exact parametrized-arc measure to the trace set.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean image of the right arc trace has \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure \(\operatorname{ofReal}(R\gamma)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the matching exact measure identity for the reflected trace.

classifications.informal_statement: The side cap has Euclidean area \[R^2\bigl(\gamma-\sin\gamma\cos\gamma\bigr).\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The circular-segment area formula applies to the auxiliary cap with radius \(R\) and half-central angle \(\gamma\).

classifications.informal_statement: The outer cap has Euclidean area \[R^2\bigl(\alpha-\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\bigr).\]
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the circular-segment area for the upper exterior cap.

classifications.informal_statement: The side cap arc length is \(2R\gamma\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The exact arc-length identity converts the side cap parameter to radius times central angle.

classifications.informal_statement: The outer cap arc length is \(2R\alpha\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The same identity applies to the exterior cap.

classifications.informal_statement: The component modeled weighted area equals the scalar formula: \(A_{\mathrm{modeled}}=A_{\mathrm{scalar}}\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The equality is the algebraic reduction of the rectangle, side-cap, and density-weighted outer-cap contributions.

classifications.informal_statement: The component modeled weighted perimeter equals the scalar formula: \(P_{\mathrm{modeled}}=P_{\mathrm{scalar}}\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The equality combines the two side traces, the density-weighted outer arc, and the bottom segment.

classifications.informal_statement: The outer cap center equals the upper center \((0,1-R\cos\alpha)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The cap constructor and the assembly center definition use the same radius, base line, and exterior angle.

classifications.informal_statement: The outer cap left endpoint is \((-R\sin\alpha,1)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The chord-radius relation converts the left endpoint formula to the displayed coordinate.

classifications.informal_statement: The outer cap right endpoint is \((R\sin\alpha,1)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the reflected right endpoint on the upper interface.

classifications.informal_statement: The left side-arc upper junction equals the outer-cap left endpoint: \[(-w-R\sin\beta,1)=(-R\sin\alpha,1).\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The identity expresses the common interface junction using \(w=R(\sin\alpha-\sin\beta)\).

classifications.informal_statement: The right side-arc upper junction equals the outer-cap right endpoint: \[(w+R\sin\beta,1)=(R\sin\alpha,1).\]
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the symmetric right-hand junction identity.

classifications.informal_statement: The entire bottom segment carrier is contained in the complete frontier of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier: \[\{(x,-1):|x|\leq w\}\subseteq\partial E_3.\]
classifications.latex_explanation: This is a frontier-inclusion theorem, including the singleton degenerate case at \(w=0\); it is not merely the definition of the bottom set.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) bottom segment equals its chord length.
classifications.latex_explanation: This includes the zero-length value at \(h=1/2\) and supplies the density-one boundary contribution in the perimeter formula.

classifications.informal_statement: The type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) boundary join set is \[\{(-R\sin\alpha,1),(R\sin\alpha,1),(-w,-1),(w,-1)\}.\]
classifications.latex_explanation: These four points contain all possible pairwise intersections of the four primitive frontier traces, with the two bottom points coinciding when \(w=0\).

classifications.informal_statement: The type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) boundary join set is finite.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is explicitly a set of four displayed points, possibly with repetitions.

classifications.informal_statement: The pairwise overlap of the left trace, right trace, outer-cap trace, and bottom segment is contained in the boundary join set.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is an assembly-specific geometric inclusion; it does not turn the unrestricted overlap definition into a finiteness theorem.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean image of that type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) pairwise overlap has zero one-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
classifications.latex_explanation: The inclusion in a finite join set and finiteness of the join set imply the null-measure conclusion.

classifications.informal_statement: The central rectangle carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: All four coordinate inequalities are non-strict, so the rectangle is an intersection of closed half-spaces.

classifications.informal_statement: The left circular segment carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is an intersection of a closed disk with closed half-plane and strip constraints.

classifications.informal_statement: The right circular segment carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the reflected closed disk segment with non-strict coordinate constraints.

classifications.informal_statement: The type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) core carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is a finite union of the closed rectangle and the two closed circular segments.

classifications.informal_statement: The complete type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: The core and exterior cap are closed, and their finite union is closed.

classifications.informal_statement: The assembled type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier is measurable.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is a finite union of closed coordinate-defined pieces, so it supports the weighted-area integral and the Euclidean frontier construction.

classifications.informal_statement: Every point of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) core satisfies \(\lvert y\rvert\leq1\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The rectangle and both circular side segments are explicitly restricted to the closed strip; this makes their density identically one.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean planar volume of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) core equals the rectangle area plus one side-cap area.
classifications.latex_explanation: The two circular side pieces contribute the same segment area, while their overlaps with the rectangle and each other lie on planar-null joining sets; hence the core volume is \(4w+a_{\mathrm{side}}\).

classifications.informal_statement: For a regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly, \[A_\lambda(E_{\mathrm{core}})=4w+\operatorname{Area}(\mathrm{side\ cap}).\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The core lies in the closed unit strip, where the density is one, so its weighted area is the rectangle contribution plus the two side-segment contribution.

classifications.informal_statement: The canonical weighted area of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier equals its rectangle-plus-cap modeled area expression.
classifications.latex_explanation: The core density is one and the exterior cap density is \(\lambda\) away from its interface chord; the carrier decomposition therefore agrees with the stored modeled calculation.

classifications.informal_statement: The canonical weighted area of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier equals its scalar area formula.
classifications.latex_explanation: Substituting the angle term and sine gap into the geometric decomposition gives the analytic expression used as \(A_3(h)\).

classifications.informal_statement: The bottom segment carrier is closed.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is defined by the equality \(y=-1\) and the closed bound \(\lvert x\rvert\leq w\).

classifications.informal_statement: The declared boundary trace is the union of the two strip-side arc traces, the upper cap arc trace, and the bottom segment.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the candidate set for the complete frontier; the two inclusion theorems prove that it is exactly the topological frontier.

classifications.informal_statement: The complete frontier of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier is contained in the declared boundary trace.
classifications.latex_explanation: No boundary component occurs outside the two side arcs, upper cap arc, and bottom segment.

classifications.informal_statement: Every declared type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) boundary trace lies in the complete frontier.
classifications.latex_explanation: Each circular or horizontal component contains points approached from both the carrier and its complement, including the degenerate-join convention.

classifications.informal_statement: The complete frontier of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier equals its boundary trace.
classifications.latex_explanation: Combining both inclusions gives the exact set-theoretic frontier needed for canonical perimeter.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean realization of the bottom segment is measurable.
classifications.latex_explanation: It is the image of a compact horizontal interval under the coordinate homeomorphism.

classifications.informal_statement: The Euclidean frontier of the realized type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier is the realization of those four boundary components.
classifications.latex_explanation: The coordinate frontier equality transports through the homeomorphism and identifies the Euclidean Hausdorff-measure domain.

classifications.informal_statement: The canonical complete-frontier weighted perimeter of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier equals its modeled component perimeter.
classifications.latex_explanation: The frontier decomposition, exact Hausdorff lengths, density integrals, and null finite joins show that no hidden chord or extra boundary is counted.

classifications.informal_statement: The canonical weighted perimeter of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier equals its scalar perimeter formula.
classifications.latex_explanation: The geometric expression becomes \(P_3(h)\) after the principal-angle identities and the common-radius relation are substituted.

classifications.informal_statement:
For every regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly with density \(\lambda>1\), curvature \(0<h<1\), and coordinate carrier \(E_3\), the strip density is Lebesgue integrable on the carrier:

\[
f_\lambda\in L^1(E_3,\mathcal L^2).
\]
classifications.latex_explanation: The carrier is the union of the strip core and the upper cap. The core has finite Lebesgue measure, so the bounded strip density is integrable there; cap integrability gives integrability on the union. This establishes that the carrier-derived weighted area is a genuine finite integral, not a formal scalar assignment. Integrability against the complete-frontier measure, needed for weighted perimeter, is a separate assertion.

classifications.informal_statement: The strip density is integrable against the complete-frontier measure of the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: The frontier is a finite union of measurable circular traces and a horizontal segment with finite Euclidean \(\mathcal H^1\)-measure, so the bounded two-valued density has a finite integral.

classifications.informal_statement: A modeled competitor realization pairs an admissible competitor with proof that its carrier is exactly the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier.
classifications.latex_explanation: This structure prevents the scalar comparison from bypassing the carrier-based semantics of minimality.

classifications.informal_statement: Given an existing realization \(\mathcal R\) containing an admissible competitor \(F\) with carrier \(E_3\), the extracted competitor is \(\mathcal R.\operatorname{competitor}=F\).
classifications.latex_explanation: This declaration is an extraction from a supplied realization. It does not assert that a realization exists; existence is a separate proposition.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized admissible competitor has weighted area equal to the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) scalar area.
classifications.latex_explanation: The carrier equality lets the common competitor definition use the geometric carrier integral, after which the area formula theorem applies.

classifications.informal_statement: The realized admissible competitor has weighted perimeter equal to the type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) scalar perimeter.
classifications.latex_explanation: The same carrier equality and complete-frontier perimeter theorem transfer the geometric perimeter value to the admissible competitor.

classifications.informal_statement: The type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier has an admissible competitor realization with the same carrier and the stated scalar area and perimeter.
classifications.latex_explanation: This is the bridge from the constructed coordinate set to the common admissible-competitor type used by the candidate minimality predicate.

classifications.informal_statement: Every regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly has an admissible competitor realization.
classifications.latex_explanation: The carrier is measurable, the density is integrable over its area and frontier, and its carrier can therefore be packaged in the common admissible-competitor type.

classifications.informal_statement: An equal-area regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) assembly with smaller scalar perimeter refutes minimality of the four-arc candidate.
classifications.latex_explanation: The theorem instantiates the candidate's universal admissible-competitor quantifier with the realized type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier.

classifications.informal_statement: For every \(\lambda>1\), \(A_3(1/2)=2\pi(\lambda+1)\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The shape is zero, both relevant angles are semicircular, and the displacement vanishes, giving a finite exact endpoint for the bracketing argument.
Bounding the outer angle by \(\pi\) and the displacement by one gives \(A_4(1)\leq2\lambda\pi+\pi+2<2\pi(\lambda+1)\).

classifications.informal_statement: Every stationary \(s\in(1/2,1)\) at density \(\lambda>1\) admits a stationary equal-area pair with type-\(\mathrm{iv}\) member \(s\) and type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) member \(r<s\).
classifications.latex_explanation: The inequalities \(A_3(s)<A_4(s)\leq A_4(1)<A_3(1/2)\) and continuity give \(1/2<r<s\) with exact equal area.

classifications.informal_statement: For every \(\lambda>1\), there exists a stationary equal-area pair with \(r<s\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Choose the regular fold zero in \((9/10,1)\), then apply the equal-area bracketing theorem.

classifications.informal_statement: For every \(\lambda>1\), some stationary equal-area pair satisfies \(F_3(r)<0\), \(P_3(r)<P_4(s)\), and \(G(r,s)<0\).
classifications.latex_explanation: Root order gives the negative fold and strict perimeter comparison; the exact stationary gap identity gives the reduced-gap sign. No numerical density subdivision is required.

classifications.informal_statement: For every \(\lambda>1\), a modeled four-arc candidate satisfying the formal CMV hypotheses is not a weighted-perimeter minimizer.
classifications.latex_explanation: The candidate has \(0<h\leq1\), \(0<\alpha<\pi/2\), and \(\lambda\cos\alpha=h\). The universal stationary pair and envelope provide an admissible regular type-\(\mathrm{iii}\) carrier with equal weighted area and smaller complete-frontier weighted perimeter; source normalization and reduced-boundary compatibility are not conclusions.
